questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always been interested in how it is studying veterinary medicine in other countries. Now that i got a possibility to do it and on the same time being with my family who lives i NL, it would be an amazing opppotunity. Utrecht is also known for as one of the best in veterinary medicine and especially in farm animals.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard before the meeting. You get one online meeting before starting and there you get all the information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing. Got a bag from the university with some folders but no tour around the school or anything like that. They also looked confused when i arrived at the reception where the international office had sent me so i don't think that they knew i was coming.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived with family

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't live to far from the university. If possible stay in Utrecht city to be close to the school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is no housing available through the uni

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They offered me some other courses than normal, because i could speek dutch so that was very nice of them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got a contact person who helped me a lot, she answered all my questions regarding registration and all the practicalities and sent my schedule prior to my arrival in Utrecht.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I got the final confirmation late but that was ok as long as i got the courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use your contact person from the host institution. They can help you with most of your questions and wishes regarding your exchange. 
Don't be afraid to contact people with questions!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were of very high quality. The teaching was very evidence-based and you work with specialists in every department.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more practical teaching in the farm animal hospital. You get very sick cows from the farmers and then you have the responsbility to save that cow. You have free hands to do whatever you want as long as you have evidence behind it and the teacher/veterinarian agrees. Beside the practical teaching we have once a week where we could choose a subject we wanted to discuss, where we sat down 1-1,5 hour to discuss.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Dairy Health Management for 5 weeks and then Farm Animal Clinic for 5 weeks.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If they were available on english i would reccomend both of them as they have way more in depth teaching about farm animals compared with Denmark

questions.answer: All the tourist stuff. It's a lot if you're doing it in 10 weeks and not just for a weekend

questions.answer: Public transportation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't get any information about all this. I had courses with student who were really busy all the time so it was first in the end that i got to know the student association club (DSK)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No idea beside DSK and the sportsclub close by

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visit DSK og join the sports club!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Bicycle alot! Utrecht, Leiden, Amsterdam. If you're coming in the spring then go to Keukenhof to se the tulips

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quit similar as Denmark so no problem!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and not afraid to ask a lot about things happening around. Maybe they then will ask you to go with them. Dutch people are very sweet people and love to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were generally very nice and helpful and the teachers were very interested to hear about Denmark and what differences we have across countries.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask for help. Say yes to everything if the teachers ask who wants to do the procedure. It helps that you don't know the people so if you fuck up, you don't have to see them again haha. Joke aside, try everything because here you have the opportunity to!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be adaptive to their learning. They know some stuff that we have not had any teaching in at all but den remember to ask the teacher about it bc they love to explain it and it opens a discussion with the other students too. The teachers rather want you to ask than to be quit

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the practical skills i have developed and the knowledge that i wouldn't have if i stayed in Denmark

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing everything in dutch while we have learned all our veterinary terms in danish and in NL they have learned it in dutch. Also i got an exam that i failed the first time because their knowledge is so different.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
